lines: \subsubsection{Configuration B: comparison with Random, Pow-D and AHIBCS}

-FedFACS reaches accuracies of 87.1\%, 54.3\% and 95.3\% on FMNIST, CIFAR-10 and COVID-19, against 85.9\%, 53.1\% and 94.8\% for AHIBCS (Fig.~\ref{fig:cfgB}). The absolute gains are 1.2, 1.2 and 0.5 percentage points (pp), equivalent to relative gains of 1.40\%, 2.26\% and 0.53\%. Over the other two methods the accuracy of FedFACS is higher by 5.5 pp (Random) and 3.6 pp (Pow-D) on FMNIST, 3.0 pp and 5.3 pp on CIFAR-10 and 3.6 pp and 2.2 pp on COVID-19. At accuracy targets of 83\%, 50\% and 91\%, FedFACS requires 35, 151 and 103 rounds against 27, 144 and 110 for AHIBCS (Table~\ref{tab:cfgB}). Cumulative uploads are 266, 1{,}381 and 1{,}047 against 270, 1{,}440 and 1{,}100, that is 1.5\%, 4.1\% and 4.8\% fewer. FedFACS therefore uploads less in all three cases but needs 29.6\% more rounds on FMNIST and 4.9\% more on CIFAR-10; only on COVID-19 (6.4\% fewer rounds) does it also converge faster. A small reduction in uploads on FMNIST thus comes with a substantial increase in rounds. On COVID-19 recall is 0.934 against 0.948 for AHIBCS, while F1 is 0.950 against 0.945 (Table~\ref{tab:prf}). Mean cohort sizes (uploads per round) are 7.6, 9.1 and 10.2 for FedFACS on FMNIST, CIFAR-10 and COVID-19. A mean of 7.6 requires at least one round with fewer than 8 clients and a mean of 10.2 requires at least one round with more than 10, so Configuration~B must have used bounds different from the $(8,10)$ of the Configuration~A ablation; the actual bounds and the per-round cohort sizes were not recorded. The fewer-uploads result must also be separated from the effect of reaching a target in fewer rounds: on COVID-19 both contribute, whereas on FMNIST and CIFAR-10 the saving comes from smaller per-round cohorts despite more rounds. Fig.~\ref{fig:cfgB} reports values from the original evaluation; Fig.~\ref{fig:gain} is redrawn to label gains in absolute percentage points (the earlier version labelled the axis as relative gain).

\subsubsection{Configuration C: fairness under noisy and non-IID data}

Table~\ref{tab:c} reports accuracy under S3 and S4 and Fig.~\ref{fig:jfi} the corresponding JFI. FedFACS has the highest accuracy in four of six settings and is below FedFairCS in two (CIFAR-10 S3: 55.85 vs 56.15; FMNIST S4 with 20\% noise: 83.11 vs 83.27); margins elsewhere are 0.09--0.36 points. Its JFI is higher than that of FedFairCS in five of six settings, by $+0.006$ to $+0.026$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:jfidiff}), and lower on FMNIST S3 (0.771 vs 0.776, $-0.005$). Averaged over scenarios, the JFI differences correspond to relative changes of 1.29\% (CIFAR-10) and 1.47\% (FMNIST), including the negative FMNIST S3 difference. These differences are small relative to the run-to-run variability that single runs cannot quantify, they are computed on the quality-adjusted index of Eq.~\eqref{eq:jfi}, and they do not show that every client is served or that per-client accuracy is more equal.

lines: -Two properties of this design should be stated plainly. First, Eq.~\eqref{eq:prio} combines $a_i^t\KL_i^t$ and $(1-a_i^t)F_i^t$ on their original numerical scales. Since $F_i^t\ge 1$ while $\KL_i^t$ is typically much smaller than one, the fairness term can dominate the priority over most of the range of $a_i^t$, which limits the practical influence of the controller; rescaling both terms to a common range before mixing would address this but was not evaluated. Second, Eq.~\eqref{eq:a} is a bounded exponential-moving-average feedback rule. lines: \item \textbf{Communication and computation.} Only cumulative uploads were counted. All candidates download the model, train and score each round, and the corresponding downlink bytes, training steps, scoring passes and wall-clock time were not measured; the accounting of Eq.~\eqref{eq:btotal} is a definition, not a result.

\item \textbf{Fairness evidence.} JFI is quality-adjusted. Selection-frequency distributions, maximum waiting times, cumulative aggregation influence, the proportion of never-selected clients and per-client or worst-client accuracy were not recorded.

\item \textbf{Baselines.} For each baseline it is not stated whether results were reproduced in our implementation or taken from the cited publication under its own architecture and preprocessing. Oort, FedCor, q-FFL/AFL, SCAFFOLD and FedNova are discussed but not evaluated, and there is no controlled head-to-head comparison against AHIBCS, FedFairCS and Zhai et al.\ in one framework.

-\item \textbf{Implementation details not recorded.} The ResNet-18 pretraining checkpoint and preprocessing, the values of $\mu$ and $B$, the Configuration~B and~C cohort bounds and per-round cohort logs, the corruption process of S3 and S4, the COVID-19 dataset version, class counts, splits and patient-level grouping, and the averaging convention of recall and F1 were not recorded.

+\item \textbf{Implementation details not recorded.} The ResNet-18 pretraining checkpoint and preprocessing, the values of $\lambda$, $\mu$ and $B$, the Configuration~B and~C cohort bounds and per-round cohort logs, the corruption process of S3 and S4, the COVID-19 dataset version, class counts, splits and patient-level grouping, and the averaging convention of recall and F1 were not recorded.
\item \textbf{Scale and setting.} At most 100 simulated clients in a synchronous setting were used. Claims of scalability or deployment are not supported.
\item \textbf{Trust.} Client-reported scores are not verified (Section~\ref{sec4.10}); robustness to adversarial or Byzantine clients is unexplored.

\item \textbf{Reproducibility.} The code and dataset partitions behind the reported numbers are not available. A future package should contain configuration files, partition identifiers, seeds, per-round scores, cohort selections, aggregation weights and metric outputs.

import re,os
t=open('main.tex',encoding='utf8').read()
b=open('sn-bibliography.bib',encoding='utf8').read()
body=re.sub(r'(?m)(?<!\\)%.*$','',t)
# environments
from collections import Counter
beg=Counter(re.findall(r'\\begin\{(\w+\*?)\}',body)); end=Counter(re.findall(r'\\end\{(\w+\*?)\}',body))
print('env mismatch:',{k:(beg[k],end[k]) for k in set(beg)|set(end) if beg[k]!=end[k]})
# braces
d=0;bad=None
for i,ch in enumerate(re.sub(r'\\[{}]','',body)):
    d+= ch=='{'; d-= ch=='}'
    if d<0 and bad is None: bad=i
print('brace depth end:',d,'first negative at',bad)
# cites
keys=set(re.findall(r'@\w+\{([^,]+),',b))
cited=set()
for m in re.findall(r'\\cite\w*\{([^}]+)\}',body):
    cited|={k.strip() for k in m.split(',')}
print('undefined cites:',sorted(cited-keys))
print('bib entries unused:',sorted(keys-cited))
# labels
labs=set(re.findall(r'\\label\{([^}]+)\}',body))
refs=set()
for m in re.findall(r'\\(?:ref|eqref)\{([^}]+)\}',body): refs.add(m)
print('undefined refs:',sorted(refs-labs)); print('unreferenced labels:',sorted(labs-refs))
# figures
figs=re.findall(r'\\includegraphics(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\{([^}]+)\}',body)
print('missing figs:',[f for f in figs if not os.path.exists(f)], 'n figs',len(figs))
# abstract words
a=re.search(r'\\abstract\{(.*?)\}\n\n\\keywords',body,re.S).group(1)
a=re.sub(r'\\[a-zA-Z]+\{?|[{}$~\\]','',a); print('abstract words:',len(a.split()))
print('todo markers:',len(re.findall(r'\\todo\{',body)))
EOF

const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, HeadingLevel } = require("docx");

const children = [];
const P = (text, o = {}) => new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text, ...o })], spacing: { after: 100 } });
const H = (text, level) => new Paragraph({ text, heading: level, spacing: { before: 260, after: 120 }, keepNext: true });

// kind: "fixed" = corrected in the text/math; "disclosed" = cannot be resolved without new experiments or lost materials
const items = [
  // ---------------- Reviewer 1 ----------------
  ["R1-01", "Eq. (7) never increments the idle counter, so the fairness term is constant.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.3",
   "The update is corrected: a non-selected client's counter increases by one and a selected client's resets to zero. Initialisation, update timing and the population mean are stated, and the range 1 <= F < N+1 is given. Whether the original implementation already incremented the counter cannot be verified; this is disclosed in Sec. 5.4 and Limitation 1."],
  ["R1-02", "Eq. (8) is not well defined; the claimed direction of the feedback does not follow; λ and F are undefined; 'Lyapunov-inspired' is unjustified.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.4",
   "The denominator is now λF + |ν(ΔKL−F)|, strictly positive since F >= 1 and λ > 0; λ = 1, β = 0.9 and a(0) = 0.5 are specified; the text states that the sign depends jointly on ν and (ΔKL−F). The rule is described as a bounded moving-average feedback heuristic; no Lyapunov function or stability proof is claimed. Whether the original experiments used these λ and a(0) values is not recorded (Sec. 5.2)."],
  ["R1-03", "Stability scores can be negative; Eq. (18) can divide by zero; Eqs. (4)/Alg. 2 and Eqs. (17)–(18) differ.", "fixed", "Sec. 3, Sec. 4.7",
   "A single aggregation rule is now used throughout: positive parts of the scores are normalised, with registered sample-count weights when no score is positive. Weights are nonnegative and sum to one; identical-model and near-zero-denominator cases are covered. The rule is stated to be a design choice whose effect was not isolated experimentally."],
  ["R1-04", "The utility is disagreement, not an expected KL reduction; the divergence computation is unspecified; the claim needs direct evidence.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.2, Limitation 4",
   "The abstract, introduction and Sec. 4.2 no longer claim an expected reduction. The per-example KL, class dimension, batch averaging, timing and evaluation examples are specified. The manuscript states that KL is a heuristic disagreement indicator and that its correlation with held-out loss change was not tested; that test needs experiments we cannot currently run."],
  ["R1-05", "The variance penalty does not separate noise from heterogeneity; scoring-batch details and B < 2 are unspecified.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.2, Limitation 4, 9",
   "The text now states only what the variance measures, that B >= 2 batches are needed and that the value is not silently replaced by zero. The batch count, sampling and sensitivity to B and μ were not recorded or studied and are disclosed; whether the penalty discriminates corrupted from heterogeneous-but-useful updates was not tested."],
  ["R1-06", "Eqs. (15)–(16) can give negative, non-integer or out-of-range cohorts.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.5, 4.6",
   "The loss reduction is defined causally with a positive-denominator condition; the cohort uses a clipped ratio, half-up rounding and clamping to [C_min, C_max]; initialisation and unchanged/increasing loss select C_max; insufficient reports cancel the attempt. The rule is described as a heuristic, not an optimal cohort."],
  ["R1-07", "The reference trajectory depends on a prior baseline run; calibration cost and test-set leakage are unaddressed.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.5",
   "The reference is now an exponential moving average of FedFACS's own earlier loss reductions; no competing trajectory, prior run, γ or test data is used, and B_cal = 0 in the accounting of Eq. (23). Because the original experiments may have used the old reference, see Sec. 5.4."],
  ["R1-08", "Counting only aggregated updates does not establish lower communication; candidates still download, train and score.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.1, 5.3, Limitation 6",
   "The protocol now states that all N candidates download, train and score and that only selected clients upload. Candidate, trained, uploading and aggregated clients are distinguished and a total-communication accounting is defined (Eq. 23). The claim is restricted to uploads. Total bytes, compute and time were not measured and cannot be reported without re-running the experiments."],
  ["R1-09", "JFI is applied to p/q, so JFI = 1 is not equal participation; 0.5 is unjustified; 0.9 can occur with 10% never served.", "fixed", "Sec. 5.3",
   "The interpretation is corrected exactly as the reviewer describes: JFI = 1 means participation proportional to quality; the minimum is 1/n; 0.5 is a convention; the 90-of-100 example is given; the quality-selection confound is stated."],
  ["R1-10", "Starvation prevention and bias claims exceed the evidence.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.3, 5.5.4, 6 (Limitation 7), 7",
   "Claims of preventing starvation or bias are removed; the manuscript states that the rule imposes no maximum waiting time and that the controller can weaken the fairness term. Selection-frequency distributions, maximum waits, aggregation influence and worst-client accuracy were not recorded and are disclosed."],
  ["R1-11", "The relation between the aggregation rule and the objective, and the completeness of Eq. (3), are unclear.", "fixed", "Sec. 3",
   "Eq. (3) is now a complete cardinality-constrained selection rule with tie-breaking. The text separates the reference objective (Eq. 1) from the ranking heuristic and states that the stability weights replace sample-size weights without a proof that F is minimised."],
  ["R1-12", "Novelty beyond combining adaptive mechanisms is not established; direct comparison with Zhai et al., AHIBCS and FedFairCS is requested.", "disclosed", "Sec. 2.4, Limitation 8",
   "Sec. 2.4 now compares decision rules and information requirements with the closest methods and states the additional cost FedFACS imposes (all candidates train and score). The contribution list is rewritten without optimality or superiority claims. A controlled head-to-head comparison of rules, information and measured cost requires new experiments and is disclosed."],
  ["R1-13", "The ablation does not isolate the utility, fairness, penalty, controller or reference.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.5.1, Limitation 3",
   "The text states exactly what A1/A2 vary (cohort sizing and aggregation) and that they do not isolate the listed components, notes that the full method is not best in every cell (FMNIST S1 alpha = 0.5: 99 vs 97 rounds; FMNIST S2 accuracy 83.80 vs 83.81) and that A1 alone is slower than Zhai et al. on CIFAR-10 and MNIST S2. Targeted ablations require new runs."],
  ["R1-14", "Baseline provenance, comparability and the Pow-D/FedProx naming need clarification.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.2, Limitation 8",
   "The methods compared in each configuration and their settings are listed, and results are interpreted only within a configuration. The Configuration B naming is corrected to Pow-D throughout. Whether each baseline number was reproduced or taken from its publication is not recorded and is disclosed."],
  ["R1-15", "No independent runs or uncertainty; endpoint definitions are unclear.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.3, 5.4, Limitation 2",
   "Round-to-target is defined as the first completed round reaching a declared target, and unattained targets are not treated as successes. All results are stated to be single-run and descriptive; absolute versus relative gains are distinguished. Multi-seed experiments with paired intervals cannot be produced without re-running them."],
  ["R1-16", "Implementation details (ResNet-18 checkpoint, preprocessing, parameters, partitioning, corruption) are missing.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.1, 5.2, Limitation 9",
   "Stated: architecture and frozen layers, per-dataset output size, hyperparameters and bounds for Configuration A, hardware. Not recorded and therefore disclosed: pretraining checkpoint, preprocessing and normalisation, batch-norm treatment, λ, μ, B, Configuration B/C bounds and the corruption process. We could not supply values we cannot verify."],
  ["R1-17", "COVID-19 is three-class but the head is described as ten-class; dataset documentation and metric averaging are missing.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, Limitation 9",
   "The output layer is stated as 10 units for MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR-10 and 3 units for COVID-19. Dataset version, sample counts, splits, patient-level grouping and the recall/F1 averaging convention were not recorded and are disclosed; the Table 4 interpretation is limited accordingly."],
  ["R1-18", "Table 5 participation counts must be reconciled with the cohort bounds; per-round logs are requested.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.2, 5.5.3, Limitation 9",
   "Mean cohorts are computed (7.6, 9.1, 10.2) and it is shown that Configuration B cannot have used the bounds (8, 10): a mean of 7.6 needs a cohort below 8 and a mean of 10.2 needs one above 10. The actual bounds and per-round logs were not recorded. Fewer rounds and smaller cohorts are discussed separately."],
  ["R1-19", "The discussion hides trade-offs (more rounds on FMNIST, DivFL faster on MNIST, lower JFI on FMNIST S3, accuracy not always best).", "fixed", "Sec. 5.5.2–5.5.5, 7",
   "Each cited observation is now stated explicitly (FMNIST: 35 vs 27 rounds, +29.6%; CIFAR-10: 151 vs 144, +4.9%; DivFL 28/35 vs 58/69 rounds on MNIST S1; JFI 0.771 vs 0.776 on FMNIST S3; four of six best accuracies in Table 6). The conclusion reports trade-offs, not simultaneous superiority."],
  ["R1-20", "Reporting inconsistencies (83.80 vs 83.08, relative vs absolute gains in Fig. 9, meaning of 200 rounds).", "fixed", "Sec. 5.5, Fig. 9, Table 3",
   "83.80% is used throughout; the FMNIST S2 round reduction is 2.8%; Fig. 9 is redrawn from its printed values with gains labelled in percentage points; entries equal to the 200-round budget are marked in Table 3 and described as not reached or reached only at the budget limit."],
  ["R1-21", "The algorithms should be one consistent executable account; a reproducibility package is requested.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.8, 4.9, Limitation 12",
   "Algorithms 1–2 are rewritten to match Sec. 4: reset to the global model every round, scoring after training with the unchanged global model, server-held counters, one aggregation formula, staged-state commitment. Privacy and scalability claims are restricted. The configuration files, partitions, seeds and per-round logs requested are not available and are disclosed."],
  // ---------------- Reviewer 2 ----------------
  ["R2-01", "Hidden communication and computation cost; baselines train only sampled clients; probing cost uncounted.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.1, 5.3, Limitation 6", "As R1-08: the protocol and claims are corrected; measured downlink, compute and probing costs are not available."],
  ["R2-02", "Eq. (11) depends on a baseline run; γ is undefined.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.5", "As R1-07: the baseline run and γ are removed."],
  ["R2-03", "Eq. (7) never increases an idle counter.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.3", "As R1-01."],
  ["R2-04", "Eq. (8) is ill-posed; λ unspecified; Lyapunov terminology unjustified.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.4", "As R1-02."],
  ["R2-05", "Scale mismatch in Eq. (9): F >= 1 versus small ΔKL.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.4, Limitation 5",
   "The mismatch is stated explicitly, including that the fairness term can dominate and limit the controller. Rescaling both terms is identified as the remedy but not evaluated, since that needs new experiments."],
  ["R2-06", "KL between local and global predictions measures drift, which is harmful under non-IID data; the sum over x is ill-defined.", "disclosed", "Sec. 4.2, Limitation 4",
   "The sum is now defined over classes for each example, with batch and example weighting. The text states that KL is disagreement, that drift can be harmful, and that no evidence is claimed that high KL implies beneficial contribution."],
  ["R2-07", "Aggregation weights can be negative; n_i is dropped; Eq. (4) and Eq. (17) differ.", "fixed", "Sec. 3, 4.7", "As R1-03 and R1-11; a sample-count fallback uses n_i, and one aggregation equation is used."],
  ["R2-08", "Time indexing, bounds, rounding, rounds 1–2 and N/K/C notation are inconsistent.", "fixed", "Sec. 3, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6",
   "The reference is causal (no future losses); rho(t-1) is used consistently in selection; initial values for rounds 1–2 are given; rounding is specified. Notation is unified: N is the population size, C the client set, C_k^t the cohort and m_t its size (the stray K in Eq. 19 is now N)."],
  ["R2-09", "The cohort range 8–10 cannot support '15% fewer clients'.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.6, 5.5.1", "The claim is removed; the text states that the bounds allow at most a 20% reduction and that the Configuration A bounds are not those of Configuration B."],
  ["R2-10", "Itemised numerical inconsistencies (cohort averages, Table 4, 83.08/83.80, FedProx/Pow-D, 2.2%/2.8%, Fig. 8/9, accuracy level, class count).", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.2, 5.5",
   "Corrected: 83.80; Pow-D naming; 2.78%; class counts (10 vs 3 outputs); mean cohorts computed and Configuration B bounds shown to differ from (8, 10). In the submitted PDF Figs. 8 and 9 both show 51.3 for Random on CIFAR-10, so we could not reproduce the 51.1/51.3 difference. Not resolvable without data: the Table 4 recall/F1 arithmetic (macro-recall should equal accuracy on balanced classes) and the CIFAR-10 accuracy level; Table 4 is reported with an explicit caution and no conclusions are drawn from it."],
  ["R2-11", "Abstract aggregates mix signs and units, and the 'best existing method' differs by configuration.", "fixed", "Abstract, Sec. 7",
   "The abstract now reports per-configuration results against the named comparator, includes the COVID-19 recall deficit, and separates percentage points from relative percentages. The pooled averages are removed."],
  ["R2-12", "No statistical rigour; differences within noise.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.4, 5.5.4, Limitation 2", "As R1-15: single-run results are described as descriptive and small margins are not interpreted."],
  ["R2-13", "Incomplete ablation; A1 is slower than Zhai et al.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.5.1, Limitation 3", "As R1-13."],
  ["R2-14", "Missing baselines (Oort, FedCor, q-FFL/AFL, SCAFFOLD, FedNova); unclear provenance; no numeric table for main baselines.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.2, 5.5.2, Limitation 8",
   "The unevaluated methods are listed as such and provenance is disclosed. Numeric rounds are given for all Configuration A baselines (Table 3) and accuracies for Configuration B (Figs. 8–9, with the values printed); a numeric table of Configuration A baseline accuracies is not available."],
  ["R2-15", "JFI is confounded with quality; 0.5 is unfounded; no client-level fairness; narrow margins.", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.3, 5.5.4, Limitation 7",
   "The interpretation and threshold are corrected, the quality confound is stated, the two settings where FedFACS is below FedFairCS in accuracy and the FMNIST S3 JFI deficit are reported, and the margins are described as small. Client-level accuracy variance and worst-client accuracy were not measured."],
  ["R2-16", "Scale, sensitivity and protocol (test vs validation, endpoints, stopping rule, noise type).", "disclosed", "Sec. 5.2, 5.3, Limitation 4, 10",
   "Endpoints and the split roles are defined and the Configuration C stopping rule is stated. The stopping split, noise type, sensitivity analysis and scalability beyond 100 clients are not available and are disclosed."],
  ["R2-17", "Self-reported scores are unverified, so the scheme is manipulable.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.10, Limitation 11",
   "The assumption of honest reporting is stated explicitly with its consequence, and verification mechanisms are listed as absent. Robustness to adversarial clients is not claimed."],
  ["R2-18", "No convergence guarantee or fairness bound despite control-theoretic language.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.4, Limitation 5", "The manuscript states that no stability, convergence or fairness guarantee is provided and that the controller is a heuristic."],
  ["R2-19", "'Ignores clients with smaller datasets' states the opposite of the intended meaning.", "fixed", "Sec. 4.1", "Reworded: the fairness mechanism avoids permanently excluding such clients."],
  ["R2-20", "Algorithm 1 mistitled; L_local undefined; garbled input; clip bounds reversed; Eq. 1–2 indices.", "fixed", "Sec. 3, 4.4, 4.9",
   "Algorithm 1 is retitled and its loss is defined by Eq. 2; the input is stated; clip(x, 0, 1) is correct; Eq. 2 indexes examples consistently with client i."],
  ["R2-21", "Reference issues.", "fixed", "Introduction, Sec. 2, 5.1, References",
   "He et al. is cited as 2016; MNIST and FMNIST are cited in Sec. 5.1; the irrelevant image-pooling reference and the press-release market-size statement (with its reference) are removed; the Lyapunov reference is cited only for the qualitative idea of feedback. A citation to 'Cha et al. 2022' that had no reference-list entry is removed."],
  ["R2-22", "Conclusion omits COVID-19; 'ensures fairness' and 'each component is crucial' exceed the evidence.", "fixed", "Sec. 7", "The conclusion names all four datasets and reports trade-offs, with the claims scoped to the evidence."],
  ["R2-23", "No code, splits or seeds; reproducibility statement needed.", "disclosed", "Declarations, Limitation 12",
   "A data-availability and code-availability statement is added, stating that the implementation and exact partitions are not available. We cannot release materials we no longer have."],
];

const nFixed = items.filter(i => i[2] === "fixed").length;
const nDisc = items.length - nFixed;

children.push(new Paragraph({ text: "Response to Reviewers", heading: HeadingLevel.TITLE, spacing: { after: 80 } }));
children.push(P("Manuscript: FedFACS: A Fair Adaptive Client Selection Framework for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning. Journal of King Saud University — Computer and Information Sciences.", { italics: true }));
children.push(P("We thank both reviewers for precise and technically careful reviews. Their central observations about the idle-round update, the controller, the aggregation weights, the cohort rule, the reference trajectory, the communication accounting and the reporting inconsistencies were correct, and we have revised the manuscript accordingly. Section numbers below refer to the revised manuscript."));
children.push(P("One matter affects how every item should be read. The original code, configuration files and exact data partitions are no longer available to us. We could therefore correct the formulation, but we could not re-run the experiments, and we cannot verify which of the corrections the original implementation already followed. We have not invented, estimated or reconstructed any experimental result. Where a request needs new experiments or lost materials (multiple seeds, component-isolated ablations, confusion matrices, measured total communication, per-client fairness, per-round logs, sensitivity and scalability studies), we say so and describe the consequence in Sec. 5.4 and Sec. 6 and restrict the manuscript's claims to what the existing single-run evidence supports. We understand that this leaves some requests unfulfilled, and we state those plainly below instead of presenting them as resolved.", { bold: true }));
children.push(P(`Summary: of the ${items.length} numbered points, ${nFixed} are resolved by corrections to the formulation, wording, notation, figures or references, and ${nDisc} are partly or wholly open because they require new experiments or lost materials; the manuscript now discloses them and withdraws the corresponding claims. Figure 9 was redrawn from the values printed in the original figure to label differences in percentage points. No new data was added.`));

function section(title, from, to) {
  children.push(H(title, HeadingLevel.HEADING_1));
  items.slice(from, to).forEach(([tag, c, kind, where, r]) => {
    children.push(new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: `${tag}. `, bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: c, italics: true })], spacing: { before: 160, after: 40 }, keepNext: true }));
    children.push(new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun({ text: kind === "fixed" ? "Addressed — " : "Partly or wholly open — ", bold: true }), new TextRun({ text: `[${where}] ${r}` })], spacing: { after: 100 } }));
  });
}
section("Reviewer 1", 0, 21);
section("Reviewer 2", 21, items.length);

const doc = new Document({
  sections: [{ properties: { page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } } }, children }],
  styles: { default: {
    heading1: { run: { font: "Calibri", size: 32, bold: true }, paragraph: { spacing: { before: 280, after: 140 }, keepNext: true } },
    heading2: { run: { font: "Calibri", size: 26, bold: true }, paragraph: { spacing: { before: 220, after: 100 }, keepNext: true } },
    document: { run: { font: "Calibri", size: 22 } } } },
});
Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(b => { require("fs").writeFileSync("FedFACS_Response_to_Reviewers_v2.docx", b); console.log("written", items.length, nFixed, nDisc); });

lines: \subsubsection{Configuration A: comparison with FedAvg, FedProx, Pow-D, DivFL and Zhai et al.}

-Targets follow \citet{zhai2024}: 44\%, 48\% and 44\% on CIFAR-10, 97\%, 98\% and 97\% on MNIST, and 84\%, 87\% and 80\% on FMNIST for S1 ($\alpha=0.1$), S1 ($\alpha=0.5$) and S2, respectively; the FedFACS columns of Tables~\ref{tab:abl-rounds} and~\ref{tab:rounds} coincide, so the ablation uses the same targets. Relative to Zhai et al., FedFACS needs fewer rounds in all nine settings: by 9.1\%, 8.1\% and 2.7\% on CIFAR-10, by 14.7\%, 5.5\% and 0.9\% on MNIST and by 4.7\%, 2.0\% and 2.8\% on FMNIST, computed from Table~\ref{tab:rounds}. The reduction is largest where target accuracy is reached early and smallest under the strongest skew. DivFL reaches the MNIST targets much faster under both S1 settings (28 and 35 rounds versus 58 and 69), and FedFACS trades this speed for higher final accuracy than DivFL: the original evaluation reports differences of 1.19, 0.74 and 1.98 on MNIST (it does not state whether these are absolute or relative). """Unit tests for the corrected equations. Run: python -m pytest -q  (or python test_spec.py)."""
import math
import numpy as np
import spec


def test_original_idle_counter_never_increments():
    r = np.zeros(5, dtype=int)
    for _ in range(10):
        r = spec.original_idle_update(r, np.array([1, 0, 0, 0, 0], bool))
    assert (r == 0).all()  # reviewer's point: every counter stays 0 -> F_i == 1 for all i


def test_corrected_idle_counter_increments_and_resets():
    r = np.zeros(5, dtype=int)
    sel = np.array([1, 0, 0, 0, 0], bool)
    for t in range(1, 4):
        r, rbar = spec.idle_update(r, sel)
    assert list(r) == [0, 3, 3, 3, 3] and abs(rbar - 2.4) < 1e-12
    r, _ = spec.idle_update(r, np.array([0, 1, 0, 0, 0], bool))
    assert list(r) == [1, 0, 4, 4, 4]


def test_fairness_range_fixed_population():
    N = 20
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    for _ in range(200):
        r = rng.integers(0, 50, N)
        F = spec.fairness(r, r.mean())
        assert (F >= 1.0).all() and (F < N + 1).all()


def test_mix_denominator_positive_where_original_vanishes():
    F, nu = 2.0, 1.0
    dkl = F - 1.0 * F / nu  # makes original denominator lam*F + nu*(dkl-F) == 0
    assert abs(spec.original_mix_denominator(nu, dkl, F)) < 1e-12
    a = spec.mix_coeff(0.5, nu, dkl, F)
    assert np.isfinite(a) and 0.0 <= a <= 1.0


def test_mix_coeff_bounded_and_finite_everywhere():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    for _ in range(2000):
        a = spec.mix_coeff(rng.uniform(0, 1), rng.normal(0, 3), rng.uniform(0, 5), 1 + rng.uniform(0, 20))
        assert np.isfinite(a) and 0.0 <= a <= 1.0


def test_positive_nu_does_not_imply_larger_a():
    # F>=1 > dkl  =>  nu>0 gives a NEGATIVE feedback target, so a decreases (reviewer's point)
    a0 = 0.5
    a1 = spec.mix_coeff(a0, nu=1.0, dkl=0.05, F=1.5)
    assert a1 < a0


def test_stability_weights_nonnegative_sum_one_with_negative_scores():
    s = np.array([-0.3, 0.2, 0.1, -0.05])
    n = np.array([100, 100, 100, 100])
    w = spec.stability_weights(s, n)
    assert (w >= 0).all() and abs(w.sum() - 1) < 1e-12 and w[0] == 0 and w[3] == 0
    # original rule gives a negative weight
    assert (spec.original_stability_normalise(s) < 0).any()


def test_stability_weights_fallback_to_sample_counts():
    w = spec.stability_weights(np.zeros(3), np.array([10, 30, 60]))
    assert np.allclose(w, [0.1, 0.3, 0.6])
    w = spec.stability_weights(np.array([-1.0, -2.0]), np.array([1, 3]))

"""Datasets, frozen-backbone feature cache and federated partitions.

Design (all choices are ours and are documented in the manuscript, because the original
experiment's preprocessing was not recorded):
  * ResNet-18 with ImageNet weights; conv1 + layer1-3 frozen and run once in eval mode, so their output
    (256 x 2 x 2 for 28x28 and 32x32 inputs) is cached. Only layer4 + a new 10-way fc are trained in FL.
  * grayscale images are replicated to 3 channels; ImageNet mean/std normalisation; native resolution.
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import torch
from torchvision import datasets, models

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data")
CACHE = os.path.join(ROOT, "cache")
os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)

MEAN = torch.tensor([0.485, 0.456, 0.406]).view(1, 3, 1, 1)
STD = torch.tensor([0.229, 0.224, 0.225]).view(1, 3, 1, 1)
NUM_CLASSES = 10
N_VAL = 5000


def _raw(name):
    if name == "cifar10":
        tr, te = datasets.CIFAR10(DATA, True, download=True), datasets.CIFAR10(DATA, False, download=True)
        xtr, xte = np.asarray(tr.data), np.asarray(te.data)  # N,32,32,3
    else:
        cls = datasets.FashionMNIST if name == "fmnist" else datasets.MNIST
        tr, te = cls(DATA, True, download=True), cls(DATA, False, download=True)
        xtr, xte = tr.data.numpy(), te.data.numpy()  # N,28,28
    return xtr, np.asarray(tr.targets), xte, np.asarray(te.targets)


def _to_input(x):
    x = torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(x)).float() / 255.0
    if x.ndim == 3:  # grayscale -> 3 channels
        x = x.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, 3, 1, 1)
    else:
        x = x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
    return (x - MEAN) / STD


def build_stem():
    m = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    stem = torch.nn.Sequential(m.conv1, m.bn1, m.relu, m.maxpool, m.layer1, m.layer2, m.layer3)
    return stem.eval(), m


@torch.no_grad()
def _extract(stem, x, dev, bs=1000):
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(x), bs):
        out.append(stem(_to_input(x[i:i + bs]).to(dev)).half().cpu())
    return torch.cat(out)


def features(name, dev="cuda"):
    path = os.path.join(CACHE, f"{name}_feats.pt")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        return torch.load(path)
    xtr, ytr, xte, yte = _raw(name)
    stem, _ = build_stem()
    stem = stem.to(dev)
    d = dict(xtr=_extract(stem, xtr, dev), ytr=torch.from_numpy(ytr).long(),
             xte=_extract(stem, xte, dev), yte=torch.from_numpy(yte).long())
    torch.save(d, path)
    return d


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- partitions
def dirichlet_partition(y, n_clients, alpha, rng, min_size=50, max_tries=2000):
    classes = np.unique(y)
    n = len(y)
    best = None
    for _ in range(max_tries):
        idx = [[] for _ in range(n_clients)]
        for c in classes:
            ids = np.where(y == c)[0]
            rng.shuffle(ids)
            p = rng.dirichlet(alpha * np.ones(n_clients))
            p = np.array([pj * (len(ij) < n / n_clients) for pj, ij in zip(p, idx)])  # NIID-bench balancing
            p = p / p.sum() if p.sum() > 0 else np.ones(n_clients) / n_clients
            cuts = (np.cumsum(p) * len(ids)).astype(int)[:-1]
            for j, part in enumerate(np.split(ids, cuts)):
                idx[j] += part.tolist()
        m = min(len(i) for i in idx)
        if best is None or m > best[0]:
            best = (m, idx)
        if m >= min_size:
            return [np.array(i) for i in idx]
    raise RuntimeError(f"could not reach min_size={min_size}; best min was {best[0]}")


def two_class_partition(y, n_clients, rng, per=2, min_size=50):
    classes = np.unique(y)
    held = [rng.choice(classes, per, replace=False) for _ in range(n_clients)]
    idx = [[] for _ in range(n_clients)]
    for c in classes:
        holders = [i for i in range(n_clients) if c in held[i]]
        if not holders:
            continue
        ids = np.where(y == c)[0]
        rng.shuffle(ids)
        for h, part in zip(holders, np.array_split(ids, len(holders))):
            idx[h] += part.tolist()
    if min(len(i) for i in idx) < min_size:
        raise RuntimeError("two-class partition produced a client below min_size")
    return [np.array(i) for i in idx]


def make_federation(name, scenario, n_clients, seed, dev="cuda", local_test_frac=0.2):
    """Returns a dict of GPU tensors and per-client index lists.

    scenario: 's1_0.1' | 's1_0.5' (Dirichlet alpha) | 's2' (two classes per client).
    Splits (all disjoint): server validation (N_VAL of the training set), per-client train /
    per-client local test (20%), and the official test set.
    """
    f = features(name)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(10_000 + seed)
    ytr = f["ytr"].numpy()
    perm = rng.permutation(len(ytr))
    val_ids, pool = perm[:N_VAL], perm[N_VAL:]
    ypool = ytr[pool]
    if scenario.startswith("s1_"):
        parts = dirichlet_partition(ypool, n_clients, float(scenario.split("_")[1]), rng)
    elif scenario == "s2":
        parts = two_class_partition(ypool, n_clients, rng)
    else:
        raise ValueError(scenario)
    tr_idx, lt_idx = [], []
    for p in parts:
        gid = pool[p]
        gid = gid[rng.permutation(len(gid))]
        k = max(10, int(round(local_test_frac * len(gid))))
        lt_idx.append(gid[:k])
        tr_idx.append(gid[k:])
    g = lambda a: torch.as_tensor(a).to(dev)
    return dict(
        X=f["xtr"].to(dev), Y=f["ytr"].to(dev),
        Xte=f["xte"].to(dev), Yte=f["yte"].to(dev),
        val=g(val_ids), tr=[g(i) for i in tr_idx], lt=[g(i) for i in lt_idx],
        n=np.array([len(i) for i in tr_idx]), n_clients=n_clients,
        class_hist=np.stack([np.bincount(ytr[i], minlength=NUM_CLASSES) for i in tr_idx]),
    )

"""Federated simulator: FedFACS (corrected spec, with ablation switches) and baselines.

One process = one (dataset, scenario, method, seed) run; per-round log is returned as a dict.
"""
import math
import time
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

import spec
from data import build_stem, make_federation, NUM_CLASSES

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- model
class Head(nn.Module):
    """layer4 + global-avg-pool + fc, trained in FL. BatchNorm statistics are frozen (eval mode),
    so BN buffers keep their round-start values as required by the specification."""

    def __init__(self, layer4, fc):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer4, self.fc = layer4, fc

    def feats(self, x):
        return self.layer4(x).mean((2, 3))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc(self.feats(x))

    def train(self, mode=True):
        return super().train(False)


def init_head(seed, dev):
    _, m = build_stem()
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    fc = nn.Linear(512, NUM_CLASSES)
    with torch.no_grad():
        fc.weight.copy_(torch.randn(NUM_CLASSES, 512, generator=g) * 0.01)
        fc.bias.zero_()
    return Head(m.layer4, fc).to(dev).eval()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- variants
FEDFACS_VARIANTS = {
    #                 cohort      agg        mix      mu   utility
    "fedfacs":        dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_A1":         dict(cohort="fixed",    agg="samples", mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_A2":         dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="samples", mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_fixmix":     dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="fixed", mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_nofair":     dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="one",   mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_nopen":      dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="ctrl",  mu=0.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_loss":       dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="loss"),
    "abl_randscore":  dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="samples", mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="rand"),
}
BASELINES = ["random", "fedprox", "powd", "divfl", "oort"]
ALL_METHODS = list(FEDFACS_VARIANTS) + BASELINES


class Sim:
    def __init__(self, cfg, dev="cuda"):
        self.cfg, self.dev = cfg, dev
        c = cfg
        self.fed = make_federation(c["dataset"], c["scenario"], c["N"], c["seed"], dev)
        self.N = c["N"]
        self.n = self.fed["n"]
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(c["seed"])

One process = one (dataset, scenario, method, seed) run; per-round log is returned as a dict.

import time
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

import spec
from data import build_stem, make_federation, NUM_CLASSES

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- model
class Head(nn.Module):
    """layer4 + global-avg-pool + fc, trained in FL. BatchNorm statistics are frozen (eval mode),
    so BN buffers keep their round-start values as required by the specification."""

    def __init__(self, layer4, fc):
        super().__init__()
        self.layer4, self.fc = layer4, fc

    def feats(self, x):
        return self.layer4(x).mean((2, 3))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc(self.feats(x))

    def train(self, mode=True):
        return super().train(False)

    _, m = build_stem()
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    fc = nn.Linear(512, NUM_CLASSES)
    with torch.no_grad():
        fc.weight.copy_(torch.randn(NUM_CLASSES, 512, generator=g) * 0.01)
        fc.bias.zero_()
    return Head(m.layer4, fc).to(dev).eval()

    #                 cohort      agg        mix      mu   utility

    "abl_A2":         dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="samples", mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_fixmix":     dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="fixed", mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_nofair":     dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="one",   mu=1.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_nopen":      dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="ctrl",  mu=0.0, utility="kl"),
    "abl_loss":       dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="stab",    mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="loss"),
    "abl_randscore":  dict(cohort="adaptive", agg="samples", mix="ctrl",  mu=1.0, utility="rand"),
}
BASELINES = ["random", "fedprox", "powd", "divfl", "oort"]
ALL_METHODS = list(FEDFACS_VARIANTS) + BASELINES

    def __init__(self, cfg, dev="cuda"):

        self.fed = make_federation(c["dataset"], c["scenario"], c["N"], c["seed"], dev)
        self.N = c["N"]

"""Resumable sweep driver. python sweep.py <plan.json>

plan.json = {"rounds": int, "epochs": int, "datasets": [...], "scenarios": [...],
             "methods": [...], "seeds": [...], "tag": ""}
Runs are executed sequentially (the GPU is shared with desktop apps); finished runs are skipped.
"""
import json
import sys
import time

    plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    jobs = [(d, s, m, seed) for seed in plan["seeds"] for d in plan["datasets"]
            for s in plan["scenarios"] for m in plan["methods"]]
    print(f"{len(jobs)} jobs", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    for k, (d, s, m, seed) in enumerate(jobs, 1):
        cfg = default_cfg(dataset=d, scenario=s, method=m, seed=seed, rounds=plan["rounds"],
                          epochs=plan["epochs"], **plan.get("extra", {}))
        t1 = time.time()
        run_one(cfg, plan.get("tag", ""), verbose=False)
        print(f"[{k}/{len(jobs)}] {d} {s} {m} seed={seed} done in {time.time() - t1:.0f}s "
              f"(elapsed {(time.time() - t0) / 60:.1f} min)", flush=True)

"""Aggregate results/*.json into tables with mean +- std over seeds and paired 95% bootstrap CIs.

Metrics per run
  acc_final   test accuracy at the last round
  acc_best    test accuracy at the round of best validation accuracy (checkpoint selection)
  r2t         first round whose VALIDATION accuracy >= target (None if never)
  up_r2t / down_r2t / steps_r2t   cumulative uploaded MB / downloaded MB / training steps at that round
  jfi         Jain index of raw participation counts (q_i = const: no injected noise)
  never       fraction of clients never selected;  max_wait  max rounds any client waited
  pc_mean / pc_p10 / pc_std       per-client accuracy of the final global model on held-out local data
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
import numpy as np

RES = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "results")


def load(pattern="*.json"):
    runs = []
    for p in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RES, pattern))):
        runs.append(json.load(open(p)))
    return runs


def jain(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, float)
    return float(x.sum() ** 2 / (len(x) * (x ** 2).sum())) if (x ** 2).sum() > 0 else 0.0


def metrics(run, target=None):
    lg = run["log"]
    va, ta = np.array(lg["val_acc"]), np.array(lg["test_acc"])
    mb = lambda v: v / 1e6
    out = dict(acc_final=ta[-1], acc_best=ta[int(va.argmax())], val_best=va.max(),
               cohort_mean=float(np.mean(lg["cohort"])), wall_per_round=float(np.mean(lg["wall"])))
    sc = np.array(run["sel_count"], float)
    out.update(jfi=jain(sc), never=float((sc == 0).mean()), max_wait=int(max(run["max_wait"])),
               sel_cv=float(sc.std() / sc.mean()) if sc.mean() > 0 else 0.0)
    pc = np.array(run["per_client_acc"])
    out.update(pc_mean=float(pc.mean()), pc_std=float(pc.std()), pc_p10=float(np.percentile(pc, 10)))
    out.update(up_total=mb(lg["up"][-1]), down_total=mb(lg["down"][-1]), steps_total=lg["steps"][-1])
    if target is not None:
        hit = np.where(va >= target)[0]
        r = int(hit[0]) + 1 if len(hit) else None
        out["r2t"] = r
        for k in ("up", "down", "steps"):
            out[k + "_r2t"] = (mb(lg[k][r - 1]) if k != "steps" else lg[k][r - 1]) if r else None
        out["reached"] = r is not None
    return out


def group(runs):
    g = {}
    for r in runs:
        c = r["cfg"]
        g.setdefault((c["dataset"], c["scenario"], c["method"]), {})[c["seed"]] = r
    return g


def boot_ci(diffs, n=10000, seed=0):
    d = np.asarray(diffs, float)
    if len(d) < 2:
        return (float("nan"), float("nan"))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = rng.choice(d, (n, len(d)), replace=True).mean(1)
    return float(np.percentile(m, 2.5)), float(np.percentile(m, 97.5))


def ms(vals, f="{:.2f}", scale=1.0):
    v = np.array([x for x in vals if x is not None], float) * scale
    if len(v) == 0:
        return "n/a"
    s = f.format(v.mean()) + (" ± " + f.format(v.std(ddof=1)) if len(v) > 1 else "")
    return s


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pat = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "*.json"
    runs = load(pat)
    print(len(runs), "runs")
    G = group(runs)
    for key in sorted(G):
        seeds = sorted(G[key])
        mm = [metrics(G[key][s]) for s in seeds]
        print(key, "seeds", seeds, "acc_best", ms([m["acc_best"] for m in mm], scale=100),
              "jfi", ms([m["jfi"] for m in mm], "{:.3f}"))

content.text:
The reimplementation is written, but nothing has run on the GPU yet because PyTorch (2.7 GB, the CUDA 12.8 build your RTX 5060 Ti needs) is still downloading. I'll continue automatically when it finishes.

**What exists in `fedfacs_repro/`:**
- **The corrected specification, tested.** `spec.py` holds the equations, and `test_spec.py` has 13 passing tests. They include the reviewers' exact failure cases: the idle counter that never increments, the zero denominator in Eq. 8, negative aggregation weights, and the cohort exceeding its maximum.
- **The simulator.**
  - **FedFACS:** the corrected spec plus 8 ablation variants. They cover fixed vs. adaptive mixing, no fairness term, no variance penalty, loss as the utility, random scores, and the paper's A1/A2.
  - **Baselines:** Random/FedAvg, FedProx, Pow-D, a DivFL-style selector, and an Oort-style selector. Oort was one of the baselines Reviewer 2 asked for.
- **A fairer evaluation than the original.**
  - It uses a held-out server validation set, so targets are chosen on validation data and not the test set.
  - It uses per-client held-out data, so worst-client accuracy can be measured.
  - It records full communication and compute ledgers. FedFACS pays download and training for all 100 candidates every round, and the logs will show that cost.
- **A sweep driver and aggregation script.** The sweep driver is resumable. The aggregation script gives mean ± std over seeds and paired bootstrap confidence intervals.

**Three limits to know about:**
- **Scope of baselines.** Zhai et al., AHIBCS, FedFairCS and RBFF can't be faithfully reimplemented without their papers' details, so the new comparison covers only the baselines above. A Q1 reviewer may notice the missing strongest competitors.
- **COVID-19 not included.** The dataset needs Kaggle credentials, which this machine doesn't have. The new study will cover MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR-10.
- **Tight GPU memory.** Desktop apps hold about 7 of the card's 8 GB. I'm caching the frozen ResNet-18 features and training sequentially to stay inside the remaining space.

Next I'll time FedFACS against the baselines on the real GPU and size the experiment matrix from that. It will likely be a reduced local-epoch count, because FedFACS trains all 100 candidates each round.

    def _graph_step(self, mu_prox):
        """CUDA-graph-captured SGD step on a fixed-size, masked batch (exact: BN is in eval mode)."""
        key = float(mu_prox)
        if key in self._graphs:
            return self._graphs[key]

        def step():
            ce = F.cross_entropy(self.wm(sx), sy, reduction="none")
            cnt = sm.sum().clamp(min=1.0)
            loss = (ce * sm).sum() / cnt
            grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, self.wp)
            with torch.no_grad():

        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
        with torch.cuda.graph(g):
            step()
        self._graphs[key] = (g, sx, sy, sm, acc)

        cx, cy = self.fed["X"][ids], self.fed["Y"][ids]
        with torch.no_grad():
            torch._foreach_copy_(self.wp, self.gp)
        acc.zero_()
        nb = math.ceil(n / bs)
        pad = nb * bs - n
        mask = torch.ones(nb * bs, device=self.dev)
        mask[n:] = 0.0
        steps = 0
        for ep in range(c["epochs"]):
            perm = torch.randperm(n, device=self.dev, generator=self.gen)

            for k in range(nb):
                sl = slice(k * bs, (k + 1) * bs)
                sx.copy_(xs[sl]); sy.copy_(ys[sl]); sm.copy_(mask[sl])
                g.replay()
                steps += 1
        return acc / (n * c["epochs"]), steps

import time, torch
from run import default_cfg
from fl import Sim

cfg = default_cfg(dataset="fmnist", scenario="s1_0.5", rounds=1)
sim = Sim(cfg)
g, sx, sy, sm, acc = sim._graph_step(0.0)
sm.fill_(1.0)


def bench(fn, n=300):
    fn(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t = time.time()
    for _ in range(n):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.time() - t) / n * 1000


print("graph replay only      : %.2f ms" % bench(g.replay))
xs = torch.randn(32, 256, 2, 2, device="cuda")
print("3 tiny copies          : %.2f ms" % bench(lambda: (sx.copy_(xs), sy.copy_(sy), sm.copy_(sm))))
ids = sim.fed["tr"][0]
cx = sim.fed["X"][ids]
print("client gather+float    : %.2f ms" % bench(lambda: sim.fed["X"][ids].float(), 50))
x = torch.randn(32, 256, 2, 2, device="cuda")
with torch.no_grad():
    print("fwd only (eager)       : %.2f ms" % bench(lambda: sim.wm(x), 100))
print("empty kernel x100      : %.2f ms" % bench(lambda: [torch.add(sm, 0) for _ in range(100)], 20))
print("cuda mem free MB", torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] // 2**20)

"""The matrix-multiply layer4 must equal torchvision's layer4 (outputs and gradients)."""
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from fl import init_head

def test_fast_equals_reference():
    dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    h = init_head(0, dev)
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(1)
    # perturb BN affine + convs so the test is not trivially at pretrained values
    with torch.no_grad():
        for p in h.parameters():
            p.add_(0.01 * torch.randn(p.shape, device=dev, generator=g))
    x = torch.randn(32, 256, 2, 2, device=dev, generator=g).relu()
    y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,), device=dev, generator=g)
    f_ref, f_fast = h.feats_ref(x), h.feats(x)
    assert torch.allclose(f_ref, f_fast, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4), (f_ref - f_fast).abs().max()
    ps = list(h.parameters())
    g1 = torch.autograd.grad(F.cross_entropy(h.fc(f_ref), y), ps)
    g2 = torch.autograd.grad(F.cross_entropy(h.fc(f_fast), y), ps)
    worst = max(((a - b).abs().max() / (a.abs().max() + 1e-12)).item() for a, b in zip(g1, g2))
    assert worst < 1e-3, worst
    return float((f_ref - f_fast).abs().max()), worst

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("max |feat diff|, worst relative grad diff:", test_fast_equals_reference())
    print("test_fast passed")

## What NOT to save in memory

- Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — these can be derived by reading the current project state.
- Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative.
- Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context.
- Anything already documented in CLAUDE.md files.
- Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context.

These exclusions apply even when the user explicitly asks you to save. If they ask you to save a PR list or activity summary, ask what was *surprising* or *non-obvious* about it — that is the part worth keeping.

## How to save memories

Saving a memory is a two-step process:

**Step 1** — write the memory to its own file (e.g., `user_role.md`, `feedback_testing.md`) using this frontmatter format:

```markdown
---
name: {{short-kebab-case-slug}}
description: {{one-line summary, used to decide relevance in future conversations, so be specific}}
metadata:
  type: {{user, feedback, project, reference}}
---

{{memory content — for feedback/project types, structure as: rule/fact, then **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].}}
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

**Step 2** — add a pointer to that file in `MEMORY.md`. `MEMORY.md` is an index, not a memory — each entry should be one line, under ~150 characters: `- [Title](file.md) — one-line hook`. It has no frontmatter. Never write memory content directly into `MEMORY.md`.

- `MEMORY.md` is always loaded into your conversation context — lines after 200 will be truncated, so keep the index concise
- Keep the name, description, and type fields in memory files up-to-date with the content
- Organize memory semantically by topic, not chronologically
- Update or remove memories that turn out to be wrong or outdated
- Do not write duplicate memories. First check if there is an existing memory you can update before writing a new one.

## When to access memories
- When memories seem relevant, or the user references prior-conversation work.
- You MUST access memory when the user explicitly asks you to check, recall, or remember.
- If the user says to *ignore* or *not use* memory: Do not apply remembered facts, cite, compare against, or mention memory content.
- Memory records can become stale over time. Use memory as context for what was true at a given point in time. Before answering the user or building assumptions based solely on information in memory records, verify that the memory is still correct and up-to-date by reading the current state of the files or resources. If a recalled memory conflicts with current information, trust what you observe now — and update or remove the stale memory rather than acting on it.

## Before recommending from memory

A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.
- If the user is about to act on your recommendation (not just asking about history), verify first.

"The memory says X exists" is not the same as "X exists now."

A memory that summarizes repo state (activity logs, architecture snapshots) is frozen in time. If the user asks about *recent* or *current* state, prefer `git log` or reading the code over recalling the snapshot.

## Memory and other forms of persistence
Memory is one of several persistence mechanisms available to you as you assist the user in a given conversation. The distinction is often that memory can be recalled in future conversations and should not be used for persisting information that is only useful within the scope of the current conversation.
- When to use or update a plan instead of memory: If you are about to start a non-trivial implementation task and would like to reach alignment with the user on your approach you should use a Plan rather than saving this information to memory. Similarly, if you already have a plan within the conversation and you have changed your approach persist that change by updating the plan rather than saving a memory.
- When to use or update tasks instead of memory: When you need to break your work in current conversation into discrete steps or keep track of your progress use tasks instead of saving to memory. Tasks are great for persisting information about the work that needs to be done in the current conversation, but memory should be reserved for information that will be useful in future conversations.
